canonical_statements: Sushaasan is not a grievance platform.
Sushaasan is not a complaint dashboard.
Sushaasan is not a passive data presenter for government.
Sushaasan is a governance intelligence engine.

source_evidence.title: Kausarbaug evening choke reel
source_evidence.summary: Residents clear traffic themselves while vehicles are double parked outside the commercial strip.

source_evidence.title: Illegal parking near Tribeca
source_evidence.summary: Repeated reporting around roadside parking outside Tribeca High Street narrowing the carriageway.

source_evidence.title: Roadside entrance drainage issue
source_evidence.summary: Sewage smell and degraded edge conditions reduce pedestrian comfort and keep people spilling into the roadway.

source_evidence.title: Mass society meeting
source_evidence.summary: Multiple societies report that heavy vehicles, restaurant spillover, and unmanaged curb use are compounding each other.

source_evidence.title: NIBM junction operating stress
source_evidence.summary: Intersection already handles 63,000 vehicles per day, so small curbside disruptions cascade quickly into corridor-wide spillback.

source_evidence.title: Corridor slowdown snapshot
source_evidence.summary: Live speed snapshots show peak-hour spillback concentrating near the Tribeca / Kausarbaug turn movement.

issue_clusters.title: Illegal curb capture near the commercial edge
issue_clusters.summary: Short-duration curb misuse near Tribeca and Kausarbaug removes a usable lane and triggers manual weaving that quickly turns into stoppage.

issue_clusters.title: Construction logistics spilling into public movement
issue_clusters.summary: Heavy vehicles and tanker parking convert the approach into a conflict zone before traffic even reaches the commercial bottleneck.

issue_clusters.title: Encroachment and informal market spillback
issue_clusters.summary: Temporary stalls, festival-period spillover, and unmanaged frontage shrink walking space and push people, carts, and vehicles into the same narrow envelope.

issue_clusters.title: Pedestrian edge failure
issue_clusters.summary: Drainage, smell, and edge discomfort reduce footpath usability, so pedestrian movements bleed onto the roadway exactly where lane width is already collapsing.

issue_clusters.title: Enforcement timing mismatch
issue_clusters.summary: The corridor fails because intervention does not appear at the exact hours and nodes where the cascade starts.

causal_links.effect_node: Lane narrowing at Tribeca / Kausarbaug edge
causal_links.explanation: Vehicles occupying the curb remove a through movement lane and create immediate merge friction.

causal_links.cause_node: Lane narrowing at Tribeca / Kausarbaug edge
causal_links.effect_node: Manual weaving and blocked turning pockets
causal_links.explanation: Once lane width collapses, right-turn and through movements compete inside the same envelope.

causal_links.cause_node: Construction / tanker vehicles on Mohamadwadi approach
causal_links.effect_node: Delayed clearance into the main corridor
causal_links.explanation: Approach-side delays reduce downstream recovery and feed extra backlog into the NIBM stretch.

causal_links.cause_node: Pedestrian spillover from unusable edge conditions
causal_links.effect_node: More defensive driving and slower throughput
causal_links.explanation: When footpaths fail, vehicle speed drops and effective lane capacity drops with it.
The cascade becomes corridor-wide because intervention is reactive, not timed to trigger nodes.

intervention_options.title: Peak-hour managed curb zone with immediate tow discipline
intervention_options.citizen_role: Resident volunteers and shop staff help maintain gate clearance and direct vehicles to legal holding.
intervention_options.expected_impact: 38-45% reduction in corridor spillback during evening peak

intervention_options.title: Heavy-vehicle holding zone and timed entry window for Mohamadwadi side
intervention_options.citizen_role: RWAs submit repeat violator timings and help verify whether the window is being followed.

intervention_options.title: Festival / high-footfall circulation protocol for Kausarbaug edge
intervention_options.citizen_role: Volunteer marshals and resident groups support temporary walking channels and vending boundaries.
intervention_options.expected_impact: Stabilizes footfall-driven shocks before they become jams

intervention_options.title: Signal / turning movement retiming based on corridor trigger windows
intervention_options.citizen_role: Citizens continue feeding structured evidence on exact failure windows to refine timing changes.
intervention_options.expected_impact: Improves recovery once curbside triggers are suppressed

optimized_solution.title: NIBM coordinated decongestion strategy
optimized_solution.primary_strategy: Treat NIBM as a linked operating system, not a single traffic spot. Remove curb capture first, regulate heavy-vehicle spillover second, stabilize pedestrian and event-period movement third, then tune signals on the cleaned corridor.
supporting_actions: Protect the Tribeca / Kausarbaug edge during retail peaks
Move heavy vehicle waiting behavior off the public lane
Create a temporary circulation playbook for high-footfall days
Use timed signal changes only after curbside friction reduces
optimized_solution.why_best: This is the highest-feasibility path because it begins with operational interventions already available to local authorities and citizens, while keeping larger municipal and city actions in sequence rather than acting blindly.
optimized_solution.citizen_role: Citizens become gate-clearance stewards, volunteer marshals, repeat-violation reporters, and compliance partners during pilot windows.
